definitions.explanation: A sentence-final particle expressing uncertainty or wondering, traditionally associated with feminine speech.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧、⟦{似合|にあ}う→似合う：02134_niau⟧かしら。
examples.english: I wonder if this outfit looks good on me.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{晴|は}れる→晴れる：00701_hareru⟧かしら。
examples.english: I wonder if it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: ⟦どう→どう：00543_dou⟧⟦したら→する：00392_suru⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧かしら。
examples.english: I wonder what I should do.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧、⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧かしら。⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{連絡|れんらく}→連絡：01524_renraku⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦みよう→見る：00283_miru⟧かしら。
examples.english: I wonder if he's doing well. Maybe I should get in touch after all this time.

notes:
GENDER: Traditionally feminine. Associated with elegant, refined female speech. Male speakers typically use ⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧ instead.

REGISTER: Neutral to slightly formal feminine speech. Common in:
- Literature featuring female characters
- Self-directed questions (talking to oneself)
- Rhetorical wondering

VS. ⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧:
- かしら: feminine, softer
- ⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧: gender-neutral, more common overall
- ⟦かなあ→かなあ：noentry⟧: slightly more masculine or emphatic

GRAMMATICAL ATTACHMENT:
- After verbs: ⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧かしら (I wonder if [someone] will go)
- After i-adjectives: ⟦{寒|さむ}い→寒い：00664_samui⟧かしら (I wonder if it's cold)
- After nouns/na-adj: ⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧かしら (I wonder if it's true)

MODERN USAGE: While traditionally feminine, かしら is becoming less common among younger speakers, who may use ⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧ regardless of gender. Still common in fiction and among older or more traditional speakers.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦どう→どう：00543_dou⟧かしら: I wonder how/what
- ⟦なぜ→なぜ：01484_naze⟧かしら: I wonder why
